newsitem.title: JAPAN: Ford, GM may join U.S. firms in samurai bond drive.
newsitem.headline: Ford, GM may join U.S. firms in samurai bond drive.

text.p: General Motors Corp. and Ford Motor Co. are considering floating so-called samurai bonds, or bonds denominated in yen, to Japanese investors, underwriting sources said Tuesday.
U.S. corporations seeking lower funding costs have been drawn to extremely low interest rates offered in Japan.
An underwriting source at Nomura Securities said Ford is considering a yen/dollar dual-currency bond by around early November.
A dual-currency bond pays interest in yen but is redeemed for a fixed amount in another currency, often the dollar, minimising long-term exchange rate risk.
Nomura, which would lead manage the issue, said the bond was likely to carry a maturity of three years, with a volume of around 30 billion yen ($263 million).
Underwriting sources said GM was also considering issuing dual-currency samurai bonds.
Would-be U.S. samurai issuers have multiplied since Walt Disney Co. launched 100 billion yen ($877 million) worth of dual currency samurai bonds in late May, syndicate sources said.
In recent months, corporations including McDonald's Corp., International Business Machines Corp. and PepsiCo Inc. have launched samurai issues.
Such companies benefit from their familiarity to Japanese investors, said Masaru Hamazaki, deputy manager at Yamaichi Research Institute.
"The case should be (the) same for Ford and GM. People know those names, so it should be easier for them to raise funds through private investors in Japan," Hamazaki said.

Underwriting sources estimate the volume of samurai bond issues from January to the end of October totalled 3.16 trillion yen ($27.7 billion). Of that, 1.79 trillion yen ($15.7 billion) were dual-currency issues.
